description: The ATmega328P microcontroller in a 28-pin DIP package — the same chip that is the brain of an Arduino Uno. On a breadboard it needs 5 V on VCC and AVCC, GND on both GND pins, a 16 MHz crystal with two 22 pF capacitors on XTAL1/XTAL2, and a 10 kΩ pull-up on RESET.
how_to_use: Straddle the middle gap with the notch pointing left: pin 1 is bottom-left, pins 1–14 run left to right along the bottom, 15–28 back along the top. Program it with an Arduino running ArduinoISP (SPI: Arduino 13→chip 19, 12→18, 11→17, 10→chip 1).

pins.1: RESET — pull it to GND to restart the chip (also where a programmer resets it)
pins.9: XTAL1 — one leg of the 16 MHz crystal
pins.19: digital pin 13 (SCK for programming, the LED pin on an Uno)
pins.20: AVCC — power for the analog parts, +5 V

plain.what: The brain of an Arduino Uno, on its own. With a few small parts it can run your sketch without the board.
plain.how: Put it across the middle gap, notch to the left — pin 1 is then bottom-left. Pins count along the bottom, then back along the top.
